title: Stability collaboration playbook + exec risk ledger (model-serving SLOs)
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for cross-functional collaboration to design, validate, and operationalize SLOs for model-serving (inference) workloads. It pairs tactical runbooks with an "exec risk ledger" that surfaces open decisions and impact to leadership. The doc is intentionally lightweight so teams can adopt the patterns quickly and feed back improvements.

Context and background:
- Redwood is scaling hosted + dedicated inference traffic and we need consistent reliability guardrails across environments. Typical failure modes include overloaded GPU pools, KV-cache corruption on warm restarts, inter-region fallbacks, and model-quality regressions that masquerade as service errors.
- Existing telemetry is fragmented (token-level latency traces in hosted, batch metrics in Dedicated). This playbook focuses on harmonizing signals and SLOs so product and infra tradeoffs are clear.

Scope (what this covers):
- SLO definition and derivation for core inference routes (text generation, chat streaming, embeddings).
- Cross-team experiment slate to validate SLO thresholds and degradations.
- Operational runbooks for oncall + feature teams for 3 escalation tiers.
- Exec risk ledger (clear, short, actionable items for exec review).

Non-goals:
- Replacing model quality evaluation systems (Optimize) — we reference those outputs but do not own them here.
- Finance/contracting details for Dedicated capacity.

Principles:
1) SLOs must be customer-impact driven: prioritize user-facing latency/availability on critical routes over synthetic infra health signals.
2) Observable and actionable: every SLO must link to 1–3 alerts and a first-responder runbook.
3) Incremental rollout: prefer canaries + short experiments vs big-bang adoption.
4) Tradeoffs explicit: every degradation policy (fallbacks, downgraded model) must include expected quality and cost impact.

Stakeholders and roles (RACI-style):
- Product / Hosted API PM: defines customer-facing routes and prioritizes which user journeys to protect (R).
- Serving runtime eng: recommends realistic latency envelopes and implements telemetry hooks (A).
- Platform / Infra: owns capacity policies and region fallbacks (C).
- SRE: authors SLOs, alerting, and runbooks; coordinates experiments with teams (R/A).
- Observability: configures dashboards and SLI extraction (C).
- Solutions / Customer Success: provides customer-impact contexts for enterprise tenants (I).

Operational definitions (quick glossary):
- SLI: successful request within latency threshold (inclusive of first token for streaming routes).
- SLO: target percentage of SLIs per rolling 30-day window.
- Error budget: 1 - SLO used to drive experiments and rollouts.

Baseline SLO proposals (starting point, for discussion):
- Text generate (hosted default route): p50 < 150ms for first token, p95 < 700ms, availability 99.8% (example).
- Chat stream (low-latency interactive): p50 < 100ms first-token, p95 < 450ms, availability 99.9%.
- Embeddings (bulk batch): throughput SLA measured separately; latency p95 < 1200ms per item for single-item requests, availability 99.5%.
Notes: thresholds are deliberately aggressive for hosted. Dedicated customers should have contract-bound SLOs with explicit capacity commitments.

Signal harmonization plan (30d):
1) Inventory (week 1): collect metric names and types across hosted/dedicated/private (token-latency, request-latency, model-queue-depth, GPU-util, batch-size distribution). Owner: Observability.
2) Canonical SLIs (week 2): define canonical metrics and shim exporters for missing signals. Owner: Serving runtime + Observability.
3) Dashboard & alert mapping (week 3): implement per-route dashboards and initial alerts that map to SLO breaches and error budget burn. Owner: SRE.
4) Trial run (week 4): run mock SLOs on a small set of routes and capture false positives/negatives. Owner: cross-functional.

60-day experiment slate (hypothesis-driven):
- Experiment A: Prefix KV-cache warm restart grace window
  Hypothesis: Introducing a 200ms grace window on restarts reduces p95 spikes by >30% for multi-token generation.
  Success metric: p95 latency improvement, no increase in error rate.
  Owners: Serving runtime (implementation), SRE (measurement).

- Experiment B: Autoscale policy tweak for Dedicated pools
  Hypothesis: Lowering scale-up threshold from 90% -> 70% GPU-util lowers tail latency during traffic surges with <5% cost increase.
  Success metric: tail latency improvement, cost delta estimate.
  Owners: Platform eng + Finance (cost estimate).

- Experiment C: Streaming first-token optimization toggle
  Hypothesis: Enabling early-token streaming reduces perceived latency for chat product by >150ms on p50.
  Success metric: product p50 improvement; platform stability unaffected.
  Owners: Product-hosted-api + Serving runtime.

Runbooks and escalation paths (condensed):
- Tier 1 (SLO burn notice): Alert -> SRE oncall -> runbook step 1 (check queue depth, recent deploys) -> if no quick mitigation, notify feature owner.
- Tier 2 (sustained error budget burn > 3 hours): Bridge initiated + feature owners + platform leads; consider targeted rollback or temporary throttling.
- Tier 3 (customer-impacting outage or multi-region fallbacks): Exec pager + CS notify enterprise customers; invoke capacity surge policy.

Operational play examples (quick actions):
- If p95 latency spike coincides with a new rollout: rollback canary; spin up short-lived increased pool in Dedicated for burst; run golden prompt runbook to check model quality.
- If error rates increase but latency normal: suspect model-induced exceptions (tokenization mismatch); route traffic to last-known-good model variant.

Exec risk ledger (short, specific, prioritized) — for weekly leadership review:
1) Missing enterprise telemetry for Dedicated customers (Impact: blind spots for high-paying tenants). Mitigation: urgent exporter sprint (2w). Owner: Observability. Priority: High.
2) No defined SLO for streaming-first-token semantics (Impact: product teams cannot measure user-perceived latency consistently). Mitigation: adopt canonical definition in 30d plan. Owner: Product-hosted-api. Priority: Medium.
3) Autoscale policy default is opaque across regions (Impact: inconsistent latency and cost behaviors; surprises during sales demos). Mitigation: standardize autoscale profiles and publish runbook. Owner: Platform eng. Priority: High.
4) Model-quality regressions are not wired into SLO alerts (Impact: false stable SLOs that mask quality loss). Mitigation: integration point with Optimize evals to create "quality SLIs". Owner: Research/Applied ML. Priority: High.
5) Rollback/rollforward playbooks vary by team (Impact: slow mitigations). Mitigation: canonical rollback template and canary tags. Owner: Release eng. Priority: Medium.

Communications and stakeholder cadence:
- Weekly SLO sync (30m): SRE + runtime + product + platform reps, review ledger and experiment status.
- Biweekly leadership note (email + one-pager): top 3 risks and near-term mitigations.
- Postmortem pattern: For any SLO breach that consumes >25% of error budget in 24h, require a blameless postmortem with action items.

Acceptance criteria for graduating an experiment into an SLO:
- Clear signal improvement across at least two traffic shapes.
- No customer-reported regressions in quality or correctness.
- Economic impact reviewed and acceptable within error budget policy.
- Runbook added linking the SLO to alerts and responders.

Next steps (immediate 2-week checklist):
- Week A: Observability to deliver metric inventory (owner: Renee).
- Week A: SRE to draft canonical SLI definitions for the three route types (owner: Aisha).
- Week B: Serving runtime to prototype KV-cache restart grace window (owner: Diego).
- Week B: Platform to publish autoscale profiles and cost model for Dedicated (owner: Liam).

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should we prioritize first-token latency consistently across all customers, or differentiate between interactive vs batch tenants?
- What guardrails do we add to avoid runaway cost when autoscaling aggressively for Dedicated bursts?
- How do we surface model-quality SLI thresholds that are both meaningful to product and automatable from evals?

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Consider a lightweight "SLO smoke" job that runs golden prompts through live canaries every 5 minutes and records quality + latency together.
- Explore a feature flag that allows product teams to choose strict vs relaxed latency SLOs for toggled experiences.

Appendix (quick references):
- Golden prompts list: /confluence/golden-prompts (linked above)
- Template: SLO definition table (metric, threshold, measurement window, alert mapping, runbook link) — create from this doc and store in the SRE wiki.

Feedback and edits: please annotate inline where you see conflicting thresholds or missing owners. This doc is expected to evolve into a final playbook after two experiment cycles.
